title: pilotr design specification
description: Version 0.4. A specification with no spec_version field is a 0.2 specification. The schema states which fields each object may hold and their types, ranges and allowed values. It also states which parameters each response family requires and refuses. The R and Python implementations enforce the same rules through validate_spec() in strict mode, its default, and add the rules that relate one value to another or to the implementation. Every coefficient and random-slope key names a contrast column or a predictor, a contrast has one value per level and thresholds increase. A uniform predictor's min lies below its max, per_subject does not exceed the number of items, and a unit named by a factor, a predictor, a grouping factor or random.item exists. A correlation key names two terms of its group and gives each pair once. A specification using a 0.3 feature declares 0.3 or later and one using a 0.4 feature 0.4 or later. None declares a version newer than the implementation. Names do not collide (see Names in SPEC.md). Below version 0.4, no two factors are between the same unit, and from 0.4 a within factor lists every unit of the design (see Factors in SPEC.md).

spec_version.description: The specification version this design is written to. Absent means 0.2. Required to be "0.3" or later by any design using a 0.3 feature, and "0.4" or later by one with several between factors on one unit, which 0.4 allocates jointly. An earlier implementation reads such a design differently and generates different data without reporting a problem. pilotr writes the lowest version a design needs, never below 0.3, so that the releases reading 0.3 read it unless it uses a 0.4 feature.

seed.description: Master seed, within plus or minus (2^53 - 1): R reads a JSON number as a double, which holds every integer in that range exactly and not every one beyond it, while Python reads any integer exactly, so a larger seed would be two different numbers in the two implementations.

contrasts.description: One numeric value per level, so each array's length equals the length of `levels`.

vary_within.description: The units the factor varies within. pilotr crosses a within factor with every unit of the design, so a list that leaves a unit out draws a warning, and from 0.4 a refusal. A single unit name is read as a one-element array, the form pilotr's spec_json() wrote before 0.3.

varies_by.description: "observation" (new in 0.3) draws one value per row, for a predictor that varies trial by trial. Before 0.3 any value other than "subject" was read as item-level, so a design declaring "trial" silently received one value per item.

dist.description: New in 0.3. "uniform" uses min and max, and a uniform predictor takes no mean or sd, as a normal one takes no min or max. A uniform draw consumes exactly as much of the random stream as a normal one, so switching between them does not move the stream.

reliability.description: New in 0.3. The latent value drives the linear predictor and any random slope keyed on the predictor, while the contaminated observed value appears in the data. The observed variable keeps the latent one's variance and correlates sqrt(reliability) with it. Absent or 1 draws nothing extra, so the stream is unchanged.

coefficients.description: Keys are contrast columns, predictors, or an "a:b" interaction between them. A key naming no such column contributes zero, which silently removes the effect, so validate_spec() refuses one.

beta.description: The exponential component's mean, for the exgaussian family (new in 0.3). Matches brms's exgaussian(mu, sigma, beta), in which mu is the mean of the response.

thresholds.description: K-1 strictly increasing cut-points, for the ordinal family. A single cut-point written as a bare number is read as a one-element array, the form pilotr's spec_json() wrote before 0.3.

round.description: Decimal rounding of the response. Only the families whose outcome is continuous take it, since the others are integers already. A beta response needs at least 1, because every proportion rounded to a whole number is 0 or 1.

response.$comment: One block per family: the parameters it requires and the fields it refuses, as in FAMILY_PARAMS and ROUNDING_FAMILIES of the validators. python/tests/test_schema.py and r/pilotr/tests/testthat/test-contract.R check that the two agree.

per_subject.description: Partial crossing: each subject sees this many items, sampled at random. Belongs to units.item and cannot exceed units.item.n.

slopes.description: Keys follow the same rule as fixed coefficients, so an "a:b" interaction slope is allowed from 0.3. Before 0.3 such a slope was accepted, sized into the covariance, drawn from the stream, and then discarded, which made the analysis model richer than the process that generated the data.

correlations.description: Keyed "a,b" or "a~b", naming two different terms of this group's random effects: "intercept" or one of its slopes, in either order, so a pair of slopes is as valid as the intercept and a slope. Each pair is given once, in one order only. The resulting covariance has to be positive definite; one that is not is an error rather than something to clamp.

correlated.description: New in 0.3. Whether this group's random effects are correlated, defaulting to whether `correlations` is supplied. It decides whether the emitted lmer and brms formulas use a single or a double bar, so that the analysis model matches the generative process instead of always estimating a correlation the process may have fixed at zero. Setting it to false alongside `correlations` is contradictory and is refused.

unit_ranef.description: The random effects of the subject or item unit, which take no over or n.

group_ranef.description: An additional grouping factor: the unit it groups (over) and its number of groups (n).
